narrative.northStar: Squarespace's Morais, made by a friend with taste
narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "Squarespace's Morais, made by a friend with taste"**

The page matches Squarespace's Morais demo section for section: "Spara datumet", the headline, a black-and-white photo, the date, a paragraph, Vigsel / Fest side by side, the reply button, a cream travel panel on white, the gift note, and a footer ending on a big "OSA". The reply form sits on the page, where Morais links to a separate page. It should look like someone without much web experience made it, but someone with impeccable taste. Cream and white sections alternate down one long page. Everything is centred. Headings are a plain grotesque at regular weight, never bold. Everything you read is a bookish serif. Photos are black and white. There are no tricks: no section numbers, no entrance animations, no sticky header changing colour, no ticking countdown. The only small capitals are Morais's own: "Spara datumet" and "Önskelista".

The page is warm, unhurried and intimate. Each section is one heading, a few lines of text and maybe a photo or a short list, with generous space between. Its personality comes from restraint and good type, not decoration.

Three looks are off limits: template wedding sites (script fonts, blush pink, floral clip art, gold foil), app or SaaS UI (rounded cards, drop shadows, bright accent buttons, icons everywhere) and rustic DIY (kraft paper, twine, chalkboard, mason jars). The same goes for the developer-portfolio habits the first design had: tracked uppercase mono labels and 01 / 02 / 03 numbering.
keyCharacteristics: Cream (#f5f1eb) and white sections alternate; one optional cream panel set on white
Centred column, headings in regular-weight Helvetica Neue, body in Libre Caslon Text
Black-and-white photographs inset in the column, never full-bleed
Black 1px outlined buttons and boxed form fields, square corners, no shadows
Nothing moves except colour on hover

rules.name: The Two Papers Rule
rules.body: Backgrounds are only cream or white. No colour fields, no dark sections, no gradients.

rules.name: The Colour Is in the Photos Rule
rules.body: Photos are shown in black and white (`grayscale`), so nothing on the page competes with the type.

rules.name: The Morais Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: Small serif capitals appear only where Morais has them: above the hero headline and above the gift note. Section headings otherwise stand alone, with no "01 —" numbering. The old block `label` field isn't rendered; the Text block has its own label.

rules.name: The Regular Weight Rule
rules.body: Headings are weight 400. Size and space make them headings, never boldness.

rules.name: The Flat Paper Rule
rules.body: If two things need separating, use a 1px hairline in `--line` or a change of paper, never a shadow or a raised card.

dos: **Do** centre everything and keep running text under 36rem wide.
**Do** set headings in the grotesque at weight 400 with -0.02em tracking, and everything people read in Libre Caslon Text.
**Do** alternate cream and white sections, and use the cream panel on white at most once or twice a page.
**Do** show photographs in black and white, inset in the column.
**Do** use 1px ink outlines for buttons and 1px `--line` boxes for fields, square corners only.
**Do** keep form labels and button text in sentence case, at readable sizes (0.9375rem or larger).
donts: **Don't** drift toward template wedding sites: no script fonts, blush pink, floral clip art or gold foil.
**Don't** use app or SaaS UI: no rounded cards, drop shadows, bright accent buttons or icon-heavy layouts.
**Don't** go rustic DIY: no kraft paper, twine, chalkboard or mason-jar textures.
**Don't** add eyebrows beyond Morais's two, section numbers, or tracked uppercase labels.
**Don't** add entrance animations, a sticky header that changes on scroll, or a ticking seconds countdown.
